title: Toyota Revives Scion as a Niche Brand, Starting With a Tiny Indiana-Built Pickup
dek: The KEI-01, limited to 25 mph and aimed at fleet and farm buyers, will be assembled in Indiana, with the relaunch set for the second half of 2027.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: A Toyota Tacoma pickup, shown for context on Toyota's US truck lineup

keyPoints: Toyota is bringing back the Scion name with the KEI-01, a compact four-wheel-drive pickup to be assembled at its Indiana plant.
Production is slated for the second half of 2027, with the brand initially sold through a select group of dealers.
The KEI-01 is limited to 25 mph and will be sold to fleet companies, according to the Detroit News, rather than for public roads.
Toyota discontinued the original Scion in 2016 after it failed to resonate with younger buyers, per Bloomberg as cited by Quartz.
body:
Toyota is reviving the Scion name in the United States, starting with a tiny pickup built in Indiana. The KEI-01, an ultra-compact utility truck named for the small Kei-class trucks common in Japan, is due to be assembled at Toyota's Indiana plant in the second half of 2027, according to Quartz and Automotive News.

## A niche relaunch, not a return to mass market

Automotive News reports the brand will return as a niche mobility line, relaunching in late 2027 and sold first through a select group of dealers. The truck is aimed at farmers and fleet buyers. The Detroit News reports the KEI-01 is limited to 25 mph and will be sold to fleet companies, so it will not be a common sight on public roads.

Toyota discontinued the original Scion in 2016 because it never resonated with younger shoppers, according to Bloomberg as cited by Quartz. The new effort follows a 2025 request from President Donald Trump for vehicles of this size to be built domestically, Quartz reported.

## Origins in a skunkworks lab

Don Federico, chief engineer of Toyota Motor North America, said engineering teams in Ann Arbor, Mich., set up a skunkworks lab to explore what mobility products could sit under the Scion by Toyota name, according to Automotive News. Business Insider reports Toyota announced the plan on Tuesday.

Quartz also noted a separate concept, the SxS, a side-by-side off-road vehicle first shown at the 2025 SEMA Show, which uses a turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid powertrain producing more than 300 horsepower. Toyota said it will keep developing that concept, but the reporting does not tie it to the KEI-01.

## What is not yet known

The reporting does not give a price, a full powertrain specification or a sales volume for the KEI-01. Those details are the questions to watch as the second-half 2027 launch approaches. For readers, the practical takeaway is narrow: this is a small, fleet-first vehicle from a brand Toyota is testing for a niche, not a mass-market return of Scion.

marketImpact.summary: The KEI-01 is a small, fleet-only launch and is unlikely to move Toyota's financials on its own. Its significance is as a signal of US-built small vehicles and a niche brand strategy, which investors may read as low-risk experimentation.
marketImpact.timeframe: Long term; no earnings effect expected before the second half of 2027 launch

tickers.rationale: Announcement is small in volume and deferred to late 2027; reporting gives no pricing or sales forecast.

catalysts.event: Toyota announces the Scion revival with the KEI-01 pickup built in Indiana
